description: The input closure covers the twelve rulespec-be family-benefit modules that axiom_rules_bindings.json binds. Each runs on the engine entity Child through a binding-local view. A person_role concept binding of the axiom:be mapping encodes 35 of their 277 Child root inputs (a child's age and enrolment facts), and the other 242 take explicit defaults, each with a reason and a citation. The axiom adapter omits an input the frame lacks, and the engine fails a request that reaches an absent input (engine_optional_evidence), so a run feeds every entry here. The routing bridge reads the four regional schemes' roots through its imports, and a view reads each root from the person column of the same name, so a name takes one default in every module that reads it. Nothing executes these modules yet: Belgium has no composed transport graph, and METHOD-CARD-BE's row BE-MC0 reports child benefits as not modelled at level until indexed amounts are encoded. METHOD-CARD-BE is the Belgium port's method card, the document Max rules on; it is kept with the port's notes, outside this repository.
status: awaiting Max's METHOD-CARD-BE ruling: every default is a proposal (new_default true)
work_package: PR 4a (Child bindings and input closure); PR 4b adds the graph that runs them

default_direction_rules: A status that grants a supplement or an increase defaults to not held, which gives a lower bound on spending.
A condition the law requires for any benefit (residence, nationality or an equivalent title, domicile in the scheme's region) defaults to held, for the children the scheme's selector admits.
An index or revaluation factor defaults to 1, which keeps amounts at their unindexed nominal level.
A rare status that removes or suspends entitlement (abduction, disappearance, an exclusion) defaults to not held.
A count, rank, income or period fact that a later graph node is to derive takes the value that pays the base benefit with no supplement, and its reason names the node that replaces it.
engine_optional_evidence: The axiom-rules-engine commit named in input_surface.engine (the engine that generated the committed input surface) gives these modules no optional inputs. A RuleSpec document holds no inputs section at that commit (RulesDocument, src/rulespec.rs:361-374), and none of the twelve modules carries a top-level inputs key at the pin. The engine rejects a rule-level default (RuleSpecError::UnsupportedDefault, src/rulespec.rs:91-94 and src/rulespec.rs:2411-2418), and the dense batch call collects only the inputs the caller supplies (python-ext/src/lib.rs:458-466). A plain read of an absent input fails every row whose evaluation reaches it with EvalError::MissingInput (src/dense.rs:2790-2803). The internal input_or_else node that would read a default (src/dense.rs:2805-2811) never comes from RuleSpec text: formula lowering turns a name that no parameter or rule defines into a plain input read (src/formula.rs:1400-1413), and src/formula.rs names no input_or_else node. So no root input of these modules can be verified engine-optional, and this closure classes none as such: it defaults, with a reason, every input the mapping doesn't encode.

engine_source_pins.note: The axiom-rules-engine source files that engine_optional_evidence cites by line, pinned at input_surface.engine.commit so each line citation names one exact file version.
